If the registrar asks you for a CNI, show them our notice on marriage in Portugal.' Notice PDF dated Jun 2025 listed; PDF text not fetched.

proposed_facts.fact: Civil marriage process: how and when to start
proposed_facts.value: The marriage process can be started online or in person at any Registo Civil, and couples must organise it at least one month before the chosen date.
proposed_facts.notes: justica.gov.pt fetched 28 Oct 2026 (DataForSEO, JS on): 'organizar o seu processo de casamento com, pelo menos, um mês de antecedência'. Unchanged since 15 Oct. IRN page repeats it.

proposed_facts.value: A marriage in Portugal is only valid once it is registered.
proposed_facts.notes: Heading on justica.gov.pt: 'O casamento só é válido se for registado'. 28 Oct 2026.

proposed_facts.value: After the registrar authorises the marriage, the couple has up to six months to marry.
proposed_facts.notes: IRN 28 Oct 2026: 'Depois do despacho a autorizar o casamento, os noivos têm até seis meses para casar.' Conflicts with the Australian Embassy Lisbon page (three months); the Portuguese registry is the stronger source. See conflicts C05.

proposed_facts.value: A civil wedding at the registry costs EUR 120; a non-urgent wedding held outside the registry, or at the registry outside opening hours or on a weekend or public holiday, costs EUR 200.
proposed_facts.notes: IRN 'Quanto custa?' table 28 Oct 2026: 'Casar no registo civil custa 120 €' and 200 EUR for outside the registry or out of hours. Government fee, not a WW price; Nic to confirm whether it may appear in EUR without the 'From AUD' format (open question). Prenuptial agreement fees (100 to 160 EUR) also listed; not needed for the page.

proposed_facts.value: Foreign couples present identity documents, a birth certificate issued under the law of their country, and a certificate of capacity to marry issued by their own authorities within the last six months, or a statement that their country does not issue one.
proposed_facts.notes: IRN 'Casar em Portugal para cidadãos estrangeiros', 28 Oct 2026. This is the official basis for the rule-by-passport block: the US route (no CNI issued) fits the 'statement that it is not issued' limb.

proposed_facts.value: Certificates and documents not written in English, French or Spanish need a certified translation into Portuguese.
proposed_facts.notes: IRN 28 Oct 2026. Contradicts the live page ('translated into Portuguese' for everything) and third-party pages. English-language AU, US and UK documents do not need translation under this rule.

proposed_facts.value: If a foreign partner does not know Portuguese and the registry official does not speak their language, an interpreter is appointed.
proposed_facts.notes: IRN 28 Oct 2026: 'é nomeado um/a intérprete'. Answers the AI Overview claim; the source does not say the couple must hire one privately or who pays.

proposed_facts.value: Two to four witnesses may take part in a civil ceremony, but witnesses are not mandatory.
proposed_facts.notes: IRN 28 Oct 2026: 'Podem ainda intervir entre duas a quatro testemunhas, mas não é obrigatório.' Conflicts with the US Embassy line in the research doc (two witnesses on the day). See C06.

proposed_facts.value: Couples declare one of three forms: civil, Catholic, or civil marriage in religious form; the process can be started by the couple, their attorney, or the priest or minister of a church or religious community established in Portugal.
proposed_facts.notes: IRN 28 Oct 2026: 'a modalidade (civil, católica ou civil sob a forma religiosa)'. Verifies 'Catholic and civil are legally recognised'. Contradicts the planner line 'other faiths need a civil ceremony first': a civil marriage in religious form is possible through an established religious community. See C08.

proposed_facts.value: Since Law 39/2025 of 1 April 2025, Portugal prohibits the marriage of minors, so both partners must be 18 or over.
proposed_facts.notes: CIG (Portuguese Government Commission for Citizenship and Gender Equality) 28 Oct 2026: 'Lei n.º 39/2025, de 1 de abril, que proíbe o casamento de menores ... alterando o Código Civil, o Código do Registo Civil'. Diário da República text could not be fetched (DataForSEO error); CIG states the change plainly. The planner line 'minimum age 16 with written consent of both parents' (weddingportugal.com, still live 28 Oct) and pedropulidophotography.com (2026) are OUT OF DATE. Recommend the page does not need an age line at all.

proposed_facts.value: Portuguese law defines marriage as a contract between two people, so same-sex couples can marry in a civil ceremony.
proposed_facts.notes: justica.gov.pt 28 Oct 2026: 'O casamento é um contrato entre duas pessoas'. Gender-neutral definition on an official page, but no official page fetched today says 'same-sex' in terms (Lei 9/2010 not reached). Planner (weddingportugal.com) and travel.state.gov (no restrictions on same-sex relations) support it. Keep hedged or confirm with the Lei 9/2010 text before stating as fact.

proposed_facts.fact: Anglican and Scottish churches not licensed for marriages
proposed_facts.value: The Anglican churches in Lisbon, Estoril, Oporto and the Algarve and the Scottish church in Lisbon are not licensed for marriages.
proposed_facts.notes: Planner page still states it 28 Oct 2026. No official Portuguese source found (justica.gov.pt, IRN, diariodarepublica.pt, gov.pt searched). Recommend leaving it off the page.

proposed_facts.value: Public municipal spaces for civil ceremonies are available at Lisbon City Council (Câmara Municipal de Lisboa) and Albufeira City Council (Câmara Municipal de Albufeira).
proposed_facts.notes: IRN 28 Oct 2026. Useful for the Algarve and Lisbon cards.

proposed_facts.value: The date, time and place of the civil ceremony are agreed with the registrar; a ceremony away from the registry or outside opening hours, including weekends and holidays, must be agreed in advance.
proposed_facts.notes: IRN 28 Oct 2026.

proposed_facts.fact: AU: proof of freedom to marry
proposed_facts.value: Some countries ask Australians to prove they are not already married; the most common documents are a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) or certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages.
proposed_facts.notes: Smartraveller, last updated 18 Aug 2026; fetched 28 Oct 2026. Unchanged in substance since 15 Oct.

proposed_facts.fact: AU: where the CNI is issued
proposed_facts.value: DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their own country, so couples should ask the destination's embassy whether they need one, whether it can be issued in Australia and whether it needs an apostille.
proposed_facts.notes: Smartraveller 28 Oct 2026. Neither page says which applies to Portugal (see F041).

proposed_facts.value: At least one applicant must be an Australian citizen or permanent resident; DFAT issues CNIs through Australian Passport Offices, Australian embassies and consulates overseas, and by mail; fees apply and rise with CPI on 1 January each year.
proposed_facts.notes: Smartraveller CNI page, last updated 1 Oct 2026 (changed since 15 Oct: adds the CPI note and the 'you may not need a CNI' step). No fee figure for the page.

proposed_facts.fact: AU: CNI from the Australian Embassy in Lisbon
proposed_facts.value: The Australian Embassy in Lisbon can issue a CNI; the form is witnessed by a consular officer or a local notary and can be lodged in person or by mail.
proposed_facts.notes: portugal.embassy.gov.au 'Marrying in Portugal', 28 Oct 2026 (new source; answers coordinator item 1).

proposed_facts.fact: AU: Embassy summary of Portuguese requirements
proposed_facts.value: The Australian Embassy says Portugal asks for an original birth certificate issued within six months with a Portuguese translation, an Australian passport and a CNI, that processing takes at least four weeks, and that the marriage must take place within three months of approval.
proposed_facts.notes: Embassy page 28 Oct 2026, which itself says requirements may change and to recheck with the Civil Registry. Two parts conflict with the Portuguese registry (IRN): six months to marry, not three (C05); no translation needed for English documents (C03). Use IRN wording on the page; cite the Embassy only for 'the Embassy can issue a CNI'.

proposed_facts.value: An overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law.
proposed_facts.notes: Smartraveller 28 Oct 2026.

proposed_facts.fact: AU: does Portugal accept a CNI issued in Australia?
proposed_facts.value: Not stated by any official source checked.
proposed_facts.notes: Research doc open question 1 stays open. The Embassy page says the Embassy in Lisbon can issue one but does not say an Australia-issued CNI is refused or accepted. Page copy: 'your Wedded Advisor confirms where your CNI should be issued' rather than a rule.

proposed_facts.fact: US: no CNI from the US Embassy
proposed_facts.value: The US Embassy in Lisbon does not issue a Certificate of No Impediment, because no US authority exists to issue it.
proposed_facts.notes: Full page blocked on 28 Oct (DataForSEO 407 and parse errors; WebFetch host blocked). Google result snippet of the official page on 28 Oct reads: 'This document WILL NOT be issued by the U.S. Embassy in Lisbon because no ... authority exists to issue it.' Full text confirmed by curl 15 Oct (research doc).

proposed_facts.fact: US: statement of eligibility and fee
proposed_facts.value: A US citizen can sign a statement of eligibility to marry before a consular officer at a notarial appointment, at USD 50 or the euro equivalent per notarisation.
proposed_facts.notes: Not re-fetched 28 Oct (blocked). Stated on 15 Oct (research doc curl). Fee: Nic sign-off; re-verify before publish.

proposed_facts.value: Processing usually takes at least four weeks, the wedding must take place within six months of approval, and residence in Portugal is not required.
proposed_facts.notes: US Embassy lines from 15 Oct curl, not re-fetched. The six-month window is independently confirmed by IRN (F023); four weeks also on the Australian Embassy page. Upgrade to confirmed once the US page is re-read.

proposed_facts.fact: UK: FCDO service for proof of freedom to marry
proposed_facts.value: Some countries ask for documents proving you are free to marry, such as a certificate of no impediment or a marital status affirmation; the FCDO online service shows which you might need and lets you apply and pay, and you need a valid British passport to use it.
proposed_facts.notes: gov.uk 28 Oct 2026, unchanged since 15 Oct.

proposed_facts.fact: UK nationals living outside the UK: no CNI for Portugal
proposed_facts.value: UK nationals resident in Portugal or in another country outside the UK do not need a CNI to marry in Portugal; if the registrar asks for one, they can show the British Embassy's notice on marriage in Portugal (June 2025).
proposed_facts.notes: gov.uk 'Living in Portugal' 28 Oct 2026: 'You do not need a certificate of no impediment (CNI) for marriage in Portugal if you're resident in Portugal or another country outside the UK.' The notice is listed as 'Portugal: certificate of no impediment' (Notice_-_Marriage_in_Portugal_Jun_2025.pdf); the PDF itself could not be fetched. Applies ONLY to UK nationals living outside the UK. It does not cover UK-resident couples, the main UK market. New since 15 Oct research (research doc said gov.uk had no Portugal-specific page).

proposed_facts.fact: UK residents: document Portugal asks for
proposed_facts.value: Not stated on gov.uk; UK-resident couples use the FCDO service (F045) to see which document Portugal asks for.
proposed_facts.notes: Research doc open question 2 stays open for UK residents. Third-party pages (pedropulidophotography.com) say a CNI after giving notice at a UK register office; not official.

proposed_facts.value: Australians can visit the Schengen area, which includes Portugal, without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period; under the Entry/Exit System (EES) fingerprints and a photo are taken on arrival at no cost; ETIAS has no confirmed start date.
proposed_facts.notes: Smartraveller Portugal 28 Oct 2026; level 'Exercise normal safety precautions'. EES now described as started for all non-EU nationals (firmer than 15 Oct wording). Smartraveller also notes airport delays.

proposed_facts.value: No visa is required for 90 days or less; passports must have 3 months' validity beyond the date of departure and 2 blank pages.
proposed_facts.notes: travel.state.gov 28 Oct 2026 (page last updated 11 Dec 2025; Level 1). Unchanged since 15 Oct.

proposed_facts.value: British citizens can travel to the Schengen area, which includes Portugal, without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period; passports must be issued less than 10 years before arrival and expire at least 3 months after leaving; EES may record fingerprints and a photo.
proposed_facts.notes: gov.uk 28 Oct 2026. Adds the 10-year issue and 3-month expiry rules not in the research doc.

proposed_facts.value: Parques de Sintra makes five venues available for private celebrations including weddings: the Park and Palace of Monserrate, the National Palace of Sintra, the Park and National Palace of Pena, the National Palace of Queluz and the Portuguese School of Equestrian Art.
proposed_facts.notes: 28 Oct 2026; unchanged since 15 Oct. 2026 brochure and regulations linked on the page.

proposed_facts.fact: State events can cancel palace bookings
proposed_facts.value: If the National Palace and Gardens of Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra are needed for state events, events booked for the same dates may have to be cancelled.
proposed_facts.notes: 28 Oct 2026, unchanged.

proposed_facts.fact: Heritage rules at Parques de Sintra venues
proposed_facts.value: Nothing may be glued, supported or fixed to the built or natural heritage, and smoking is only allowed in signed outdoor areas.
proposed_facts.notes: 28 Oct 2026. Smoking rule is new to the ledger.

proposed_facts.value: Roof restoration at the Palace of Monserrate runs until the first quarter of 2027, with scaffolding and a temporary covering on the monument.
proposed_facts.notes: NEW 28 Oct 2026. Relevant to any Monserrate image or 'ceremony in front of Monserrate' line for 2026 to early 2027 dates; Visual Lead and Copywriter should know.

proposed_facts.value: Pousadas de Portugal hosts weddings in historic buildings such as palaces, castles and monasteries, including the Pousada Palácio de Queluz and Pousada Castelo Palmela.
proposed_facts.notes: 28 Oct 2026. Changed wording since the research doc: the page no longer says 'convents'; it says 'palaces, majestic castles, charming monasteries, and historic buildings'.

proposed_facts.value: For beaches designated as bathing waters (concession beaches), municipalities license events and activities (Decree-Law 97/2018); on other beaches and the rest of the coast, the local Captain of the Port (Capitania) remains responsible.
proposed_facts.notes: Autoridade Marítima Nacional FAQ 28 Oct 2026: 'para realizar um evento na praia, deverá dirigir-se ao município territorialmente competente' and 'Nas restantes praias ... permanece no Capitão do Porto'. Corrects the AI Overview claim that a maritime police licence is always needed (C11). Copy: 'beach ceremonies need a permit from the local council or port authority'.

proposed_facts.value: All beaches in Portugal are public.
proposed_facts.notes: Planner FAQ (research doc, 15 Oct); not re-checked; no official source fetched. Prefer F056 wording.

proposed_facts.fact: Forte da Cruz and Palácio do Freixo details
proposed_facts.value: Forte da Cruz (Estoril) is a 17th-century beachside castle about 30 minutes from downtown Lisbon and 20 minutes from Lisbon airport, with an oceanfront tent seating 200 to 250; Palácio do Freixo in Porto is a restored 18th-century manor on the Douro.
proposed_facts.notes: The Knot (updated 26 Mar 2024), still stated 28 Oct. Competitor media: capacities need the venue's own source before use; do not use The Knot as the only source.

proposed_facts.value: Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms; a buy-out is often separate from the venue fee; fees may be per day or per guest with a minimum; venue fees may be quoted before 23% VAT.
proposed_facts.notes: Planner blog Jan 2024 (research doc); not re-fetched. Kay Northrup page (28 Oct) independently says buy-out is optional at many properties. 23% VAT not checked on an official tax source.

proposed_facts.value: Most Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the centre.
proposed_facts.notes: Planner FAQ only; not re-checked 28 Oct. Use only attributed or as 'many'.

proposed_facts.value: Spring and autumn are the most recommended times; summer is hot and peak-season travel costs more.
proposed_facts.notes: The Knot (updated 26 Mar 2024), still stated 28 Oct: 'best time to visit Portugal is in the spring ... or in the fall. The summer months can get hot'. Competitor media; attribute or pair with F068.

proposed_facts.value: Mists characterise the Sintra Hills, and Pena is often hidden under them.
proposed_facts.notes: Parques de Sintra Pena page 28 Oct 2026. Official alternative to The Knot's 'microclimate' line.

proposed_facts.value: The Knot lists direct flights to Lisbon from Boston, Chicago, Miami, New York City, Philadelphia, San Francisco and Washington DC.
proposed_facts.notes: Still stated 28 Oct but dated Mar 2024; verify 2027 routes on airline or airport schedules before use.

proposed_facts.value: The Douro Valley is about three hours north of Lisbon.
proposed_facts.notes: Still stated 28 Oct. A third-party Porto photographer says Porto to the Douro is about a 1-hour drive. Use 'a short drive from Porto' only with a source.

proposed_facts.value: The Douro harvest is in September.
proposed_facts.notes: Research doc section 4 states it with no source; The Knot does not mention September. Find an IVDP or tourism-board source or drop the month.

proposed_facts.value: The Algarve is the region of Portugal with the most Blue Flags in summer 2026.
proposed_facts.notes: Visit Algarve article 8 May 2026 (snippet): 'O Algarve volta a ser, no Verão de 2026, a região do País com mais Bandeira Azuis hasteadas'. Page could not be parsed. Counts differ by source: The Knot 2024 '85 of which have Blue Flag status'; Região de Turismo do Algarve Facebook 2026 '86 praias'; press (ipressjournal 4 May 2026) 96 awards incl. 85 coastal beaches. bandeiraazul.abaae.pt 2026 results not reached. Use no number until checked in a browser.

proposed_facts.value: The Algarve has about 200 km of coastline.
proposed_facts.notes: Competitor pages (ionianweddings, The Knot 'over 125 miles'). Consistent but not official.

proposed_facts.value: Wildfire risk is highest in the hot, dry months of June to September; heat waves are common in July and August; heavy rain is most common from October to February.
proposed_facts.notes: travel.state.gov 28 Oct 2026. Official support for a 'When to go' tab.

proposed_facts.value: About 100 guests: EUR 25,000 to 70,000; planner EUR 2,000 to 10,000; venue rental from about EUR 3,000 to 15,000 or more; catering EUR 80 to 200 per person including drinks; photography EUR 1,500 to 6,000; legal paperwork and translations EUR 200 to 500.
proposed_facts.notes: Page still states every figure on 28 Oct 2026. Publication date not shown in the parsed text (research doc records Feb 2025; comments dated Nov 2025). Allowed only as a named, dated third-party range in the Costs tab.

proposed_facts.value: Venue spend ranged from USD 12,000 (2 nights, sleeps 70, northern Portugal, high season) to USD 77,000 (3 nights, sleeps about 40, high season); one northern wedding dinner with open bar cost USD 225 per person.
proposed_facts.notes: Page still states these figures on 28 Oct 2026. Date not shown in the parsed text (research doc: Jun 2025). Prices are USD at the time paid; page says prices rise up to 10% a year. Named, dated Costs tab only.

proposed_facts.fact: Cost range attributed to Pedro Pulido Photography (2026)
proposed_facts.notes: Could not find this range on pedropulidophotography.com on 28 Oct (2026 legal guide and destination page checked; site search returned no cost page). The 2026 legal guide gives only 'Civil Registry Wedding: Around EUR 120 to 200'. Unverifiable; do not use.

proposed_facts.fact: Park and National Palace of Pena
proposed_facts.value: The romantic, castle-like palace crowning the Sintra hills; its coloured tones are the pinnacle of Romanticism in Portugal and the legacy of Ferdinand II, the King-Artist, set in a wooded park.
proposed_facts.notes: Parques de Sintra 28 Oct 2026.

proposed_facts.value: A masterpiece of Romanticism created by Francis Cook, a 19th-century British industrialist and art collector, with exotic gardens and a palace by architect James Knowles Jr.; available for private celebrations.
proposed_facts.notes: Parques de Sintra 28 Oct 2026. See F054 on roof works to Q1 2027.

proposed_facts.value: A national palace near Lisbon that Parques de Sintra offers for events, with the upper gardens and Throne Room named for event use.
proposed_facts.notes: 28 Oct 2026. 'Baroque' is not stated on the pages fetched; keep it out or source it.

proposed_facts.value: A UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape (inscribed 2001) where wine has been made for about 2,000 years and Port wine quality has been regulated since 1756, with steep terraced vineyards and wine quintas.
proposed_facts.notes: whc.unesco.org 28 Oct 2026. Replaces the live line 'one of the world's oldest wine regions', which UNESCO does not say.

proposed_facts.value: Golden sea stacks and grottoes on the western Algarve.
proposed_facts.notes: Visit Algarve page did not render for DataForSEO on 28 Oct (as on 15 Oct). Writer confirms in a browser.

proposed_facts.value: Terraced vineyards, wine quintas and river trips from Porto.
proposed_facts.notes: Not fetched 28 Oct. UNESCO (F075) covers terraces and quintas; 'river trips from Porto' still needs the tourism board.

proposed_facts.value: Use exactly: Wedded Wonderland, Wedded Concierge, Wedded Advisor, Wedded Privileges. 'Wonderland Luxury Advisor' and lower-case 'Wedded advisor' are not brand names.
proposed_facts.notes: Internal brand standard.
